followup_explanation:
I selected Plover-235B because the query is a quantitative reasoning problem — composing functions and evaluating them at a point — where raw capability matters most for getting the arithmetic and algebra right.

The deciding factor was the benchmark gap. Plover outscores Whimbrel on every public benchmark, including the ones most relevant to math reasoning: MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 74.8), GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 54.3), and Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 81.4). These gaps are well outside run-to-run variance, so they point to a genuine capability advantage on exactly this kind of structured problem.

The task preference profiles didn't factor in here — both models report flat preferences on harm-adjacent content, and this query is benign, so neither's behavioral profile created any reason to prefer one over the other. With preferences neutral, capability is the right tiebreaker, and that favors Plover clearly.
